additional_info.subject: RE: AW: AW: ID0403441-DC/Si-D/DE-[xKEehO]- Delivering less power CRM:00645000938
additional_info.body:
Hi,
We have analyzed the logs for Jan 20th and found that there was an issue with communication between the SECC and PLC, which caused the outlet to go out of order. However, after reviewing the logs from the past four weeks, we have confirmed that this issue has not reoccurred since Jan 20th. Currently, we do not see any communication issues.
However, we have noticed a high number of messages indicating that the emergency button has been pressed. Could you confirm if someone on-site is actually pressing the button? It appears to be toggling regularly, which could indicate either manual operation or a potential connection issue.
Could you please verify this from the site?
Thank you
Best Regards,
Vishal Dhiman
eMobility Support Team
Please do not change the subject line with replying back to this email.

Dear Colleagues,
I am writing to formally inform that we are moving case 0403441 ﻿from the
eMobility DC Queue (Level 2)
to the
eMobility RC-DE SI E Queue (Level 2)
, due to one or more following reason (s) :
We have checked the logs and found that the emergency button error is keep occurring even if the charger is not equipped with the emergency button.
Please plan a site visit to check the wirings related to the emergency line.
For your reference:
Reason
Applicable
Onsite Repair (Component Exchange)
Onsite Troubleshooting
✔
End Customer Communication
Spare Part Ordering
Performance monitoring by RC
Kindly pick up the case using "
Pick
" option in the queue, or manually using the "
Assign
" function from the
eMobility RC-DE SI E Queue (Level 2)
and work on it & document the activity (Logs/Field Service Report) and attach it to the Notes in the case timeline on ISP.
Later assign the case to
eMobility DC Queue (Level 2) Team
, using "
Assign
" function and then move the case to
eMobility DC Queue (Level 2)
using "
Add to Queue
".
Thank you.
